_comment: PROPOSAL rev B: 3D general arrangement, fitted to the sim's room graph (ship.json). Frame: meters; x fore(+)/aft(-), y starboard(+)/port(-), z up(+); origin amidships on the main-deck floor. Rooms are boxes. A room's local coordinate u (left to right in its side-on camera) comes from axis + origin: '+x' u = x - origin, '-x' u = origin - x, '+y' u = y - origin, '-y' u = origin - y. 'view' is the wall the room camera faces. Rooms marked new are suggestions the sim does not have yet. Hatches give 3D door points (or a path for ladders and crawls). Shafts are ladder wells, lifts and vertical vents; ducts are the crawlable vent network. tools/ship3d.mjs checks all of it.
name: Long-range survey ship
summary: A 138 m, single-occupant survey ship in the Krait mold: a flat, wide top deck over a belly that hangs below it, two flat tines running forward from the deck to blunt tips, and two big thrusters housed in the rear corners of the hull. A deckhouse amidships-aft holds the living deck, and the bridge sits in a raised tower on top of it, looking forward over the whole length of the ship.

rooms.info: Top of the tower, under a raked canopy. Helm, nav, scanner and terminal face forward over the whole length of the hull and the forked bow. The ladder from the living deck comes up through a floor hatch in the middle of the room.
Spine of the living deck. The bridge ladder rises from its aft end, the trunk ladder drops to the main deck at its forward end.
Along the starboard wall of the deckhouse, behind its longest window, looking out across the dorsal hull and the radiators. Couch, easel, speaker and room to exercise.
Starboard, forward of the lounge. Pantry, stove, counter and a table by a starboard porthole.
Port side. Bunk, basin, desk, locker and the torpor pod, with a porthole out to port.
Service spine of the main deck, directly under the living-deck spine. Six compartments open off it; engineering is through the bulkhead at its aft end.

Starboard, running outboard from the corridor all the way to the hull: ten grow trays, the algae tank, the seed bank and two pumps, with a long window in the sloping flank at the far end. The plumbing crawlway leaves from its aft side.
rooms.resize: lengthened from 12 m to 19.9 m so the bay reaches the hull's starboard flank and gets daylight through its own window strip

rooms.info: Starboard, back to back with hydroponics so the water mains are short. Recycler, oxygen generator, CO₂ scrubber and dehumidifier.

virtualWindow.note: a wall screen showing that exterior camera, in place of a real window

rooms.info: Starboard, aft. Bench, fabricator and lathe, with a door straight through to engineering.

virtualWindow.note: a wall screen showing that exterior camera, in place of a real window

rooms.info: Port side. Shelves and crates of spares, feedstock and food.

virtualWindow.note: a wall screen showing that exterior camera, in place of a real window

rooms.info: Against the port hull now, at the end of its own passage: inner door from the passage, suit rack, and an outer door straight to space that opens onto an external lift down to the ground.

Full-width compartment at the aft end of the pressurized decks. Its camera looks aft at the shadow-shield bulkhead: scoop manifold to starboard, the reactor face on the centerline, drive coupling to port.

rooms.name: Gym
rooms.info: Treadmill, rower and a resistance rig at the forward end of the deckhouse. Long voyages need more than the lounge's exercise corner.

rooms.name: Forward lookout
rooms.info: Short passage ending at the deckhouse's glazed front: a standing view over the forward hull. The freight lift opens off it.

rooms.name: Medbay
rooms.info: Diagnostic bed, autodoc arm, pharmacy locker. Near the bridge ladder and the lift, so an injured traveler is never far from it.

rooms.name: Washroom
rooms.info: Shower and toilet. The laundry is across the spine.

rooms.name: Forward service passage
rooms.info: Continues the service spine forward to the lab, the data core, the stores and the refinery. The forward ladder well drops to the lower deck from here.

rooms.name: Geology & chemistry lab
rooms.info: Glovebox, spectrometer, core racks and a microscope bench. Samples come up from the hold on the freight lift and get analyzed here.

rooms.name: Data & navigation core
rooms.info: The ship computer's racks, the star catalog and the survey archive, in a cool, quiet room.

rooms.name: Spares & feedstock store
rooms.info: Bulk spares, fabricator feedstock and long-term food, next to the freight lift.

rooms.name: Refinery
rooms.info: Crushes and sorts ore and ice from the bunkers below into fabricator feedstock and water.

rooms.name: Lower passage
rooms.info: Runs the length of the lower deck between the hold and the rover bay, from the power and shield rooms aft to the skiff bay forward. Both ladder wells and the freight lift come down into it.

rooms.name: Cargo & sample hold
rooms.info: Racks of sealed sample cases, ore drums and bulk stores, out to the belly wall with its windows. Cargo for trade or delivery work would go here too.

rooms.name: Rover bay
rooms.info: Unpressurized garage for the surface rover. The traveler reaches it suited, down the ladder from the airlock's outer hatch. The bay floor is a platform that lowers the rover to the ground and raises it again.

rooms.name: Skiff bay
rooms.info: Hangar for the survey skiff, at the forward end of the lower passage. The bay depressurizes and its belly doors open to drop the skiff clear of the hull.

rooms.name: Starboard gallery
rooms.info: A long observation walkway against the starboard side of the hull, with windows in the sloping wall looking out and down. Reached by the cross passage.

rooms.name: Port gallery
rooms.info: A long observation walkway against the port side of the hull, looking out and down.

rooms.name: Cross passage
rooms.info: Runs across the ship from the end of the forward service passage to both galleries.

rooms.name: Airlock passage
rooms.info: Runs from the service spine out to the airlock against the port hull. The sim's corridor-to-airlock crossing would grow from 7 s to about 20 s.

rooms.name: Rover suit lock
rooms.info: Small lock between the lower passage and the unpressurized rover bay: suit up here, cycle, walk out to the rover.

rooms.name: Biology lab
rooms.info: Living samples: an isolation glovebox, incubators, a culture library and a microscope bench. Anything alive from a world's surface is examined here before it goes near the grow trays.

rooms.name: Sample cold store
rooms.info: Freezers and a cryo cabinet for cores, ice and tissue samples, held at their home temperature until the labs are ready for them.

rooms.name: Observatory
rooms.info: Telescope control and the spectrograph: the turret on the deck above feeds this room. Star and planet surveys are planned and run from here, and its window looks out and down to port.

rooms.name: Drone bay
rooms.info: Racks of small survey drones and their charging cradles. They launch through a hatch in the deck to map moons and rings the ship won't visit.

rooms.name: Study & library
rooms.info: A quiet room behind the lounge: shelves of books, a writing desk, a reading chair and an old record player.

rooms.name: Power room
rooms.info: Main switchboards, the battery banks and the power distribution for the whole ship, under engineering.

rooms.name: Storm shelter
rooms.info: A small room walled in by the water tanks, which make it the best-shielded space on board: bunk, rations and a console, for solar storms and close passes of hot stars.

rooms.name: Laundry
rooms.info: Washer-dryer, a drying rack and the linen lockers, across the spine from the quarters. Gray water goes straight to life support for recycling.

rooms.name: Pantry
rooms.info: Dry stores, a chest freezer and the spice rack behind the galley: about a year of food that the grow trays don't make.

rooms.name: Sickbay isolation
rooms.info: A sealed side room off the medbay with its own air supply and filters, for anything caught from a sample or a planet.

rooms.name: Comms room
rooms.info: Transmitters, the long-range antenna controls and the message archive, beside the data core it shares cabling with. A station's mission board would come in here.

rooms.name: Science stores
rooms.info: Lab consumables, sample jars, core tubes, reagents and spare instruments for both labs, next to the cold store.

rooms.name: Armory
rooms.info: Small arms, a suit-mounted rifle and a sidearm in a locked rack, with a bench for cleaning and repair. For a ship this far out, mostly for wildlife and the odd unfriendly visitor.

rooms.name: Fire control
rooms.info: The weapons and shield computers, targeting and the gimbal controllers for all six hardpoints, with a console for working on them. The traveler fights from the bridge; the systems live here.

rooms.name: Magazine
rooms.info: Armored ammunition store with hoists to the ventral and dorsal hardpoints, and blow-out panels in the deck above it.

rooms.name: Brig
rooms.info: Two small detention cells with their own air and a monitored door, for bounty hunting or carrying a prisoner.

rooms.name: Secure cargo
rooms.info: A shielded, scan-resistant vault for valuable or sensitive cargo: data cores, rare samples, and anything a contract says must not be seen.

rooms.name: Passenger cabin 1
rooms.info: A passenger cabin: bunk, fresher, locker and a fold-down desk, opening onto the starboard gallery and its windows.

rooms.name: Passenger cabin 2
rooms.info: A passenger cabin, the same as its neighbors.

rooms.name: Passenger cabin 3
rooms.info: A passenger cabin, the same as its neighbors.

rooms.name: Passenger lounge
rooms.info: Seats, a kitchenette and a screen for passengers, so they have somewhere of their own on the voyage and the living deck stays the traveler's.

rooms.name: Countermeasures store
rooms.info: Racks of heat sinks, chaff canisters and point-defense rounds, feeding the utility mounts on the deck above and on the belly below.

rooms.name: Xeno containment
rooms.info: Sealed enclosures for live specimens, each with its own air, temperature and light, opening off the biology lab. Big enough for xenobiology contracts that want something brought back alive.

rooms.name: Mapping room
rooms.info: Survey maps and the drone consoles: drone flights are planned here and their data stitched into charts.

rooms.name: Shield generator room
rooms.info: The shield generator and its capacitor banks, beside the power room and right under engineering.

hatches.note: ladder well up through the deckhouse roof into the bridge
the trunk ladder between the two spines
a run of the under-floor crawl duct, beside the water mains

shafts.name: Trunk ladder well
shafts.info: The main ladder well, through all three hull decks at the forward end of the two spines. The sim's spine hatch is its upper half.

shafts.name: Bridge ladder well
shafts.info: From the aft end of the living spine up through the deckhouse roof into the bridge.

shafts.name: Forward ladder well
shafts.info: Second way between the main and lower decks, so the hold and rover bay are never one hatch from being cut off.

shafts.name: Freight lift
shafts.info: 4.2 m platform rated for six tonnes, serving the lower, main and living decks: sample cases from the hold, reactor spares, crates for the galley, a stretcher to the medbay.

shafts.name: Rover bay platform
shafts.info: The bay floor drops through the belly on four screw jacks, lowering the rover to the ground when landed and raising it back in.

shafts.name: Aft vent shaft
shafts.info: Vertical vent with rungs, behind engineering: joins the main-deck overhead duct to the deckhouse roof duct.

shafts.name: Forward vent shaft
shafts.info: Vertical vent with rungs at the forward end of the service spine: joins the overhead duct to the under-floor crawl.

shafts.name: Skiff bay doors
shafts.info: Clamshell doors in the belly. The skiff drops out on its own lift fans and comes back up the same way.

shafts.name: External EVA lift
shafts.info: A cage on the outside of the hull by the airlock's outer door. It lowers a suited traveler to the ground and brings them back up.

shafts.name: Starboard lifeboat ladder
shafts.info: A short ladder up through the gallery ceiling into the lifeboat's hatch.

shafts.name: Port lifeboat ladder
shafts.info: A short ladder up through the gallery ceiling into the lifeboat's hatch.

shafts.name: Lower vent shaft
shafts.info: Vertical vent with rungs: joins the under-floor crawl of the main deck to the lower deck's crawl.

ducts.name: Main-deck overhead duct
ducts.info: Air returns and cable trays in the 1.4 m void above the main deck. 0.9 m square and crawlable, with a ceiling grille into every compartment it passes.

ducts.name: Under-floor crawl
ducts.info: Crawlspace beneath the main-deck plates, beside the water mains and power trunks. The plumbing crawl between life support and hydroponics is one run of it.

ducts.name: Deckhouse roof duct
ducts.info: Air handling above the living deck, under the deckhouse roof. Grilles into every cabin; the aft vent shaft drops from its end.

ducts.name: Lower-deck crawl
ducts.info: Air returns under the lower-deck plates, with grilles into the power room, hold, rover bay and storm shelter. The lower vent shaft climbs to the main deck's crawl.

modules.name: Survey sensor array (port tine)
modules.info: Long-baseline survey sensors inside the tine, under the sensor windows on its top. With its twin on the other tine they give a 25 m baseline.

modules.name: Survey sensor array (starboard tine)
modules.info: Long-baseline survey sensors inside the tine, under the sensor windows on its top. With its twin on the other tine they give a 25 m baseline.

modules.name: Scoop processing plant
modules.info: Separates and chills scooped hydrogen before it goes aft to the tanks.

modules.name: Water & consumables tanks
modules.info: Potable water, gray water and bulk nutrient stock. Their bulk also shields the storm shelter beside them.

modules.name: Ore & ice bunkers
modules.info: Raw material waiting for the refinery above.

modules.name: Fuel tank (port)
modules.info: A conformal liquid-hydrogen tank filling the thruster housing, centered on its nozzle bank. Hydrogen is kept at low pressure, so it doesn't need a cylinder: a chamfered box with internal baffles holds far more in the same space. With its twin, about 180 t usable.

modules.name: Fuel tank (starboard)
modules.info: A conformal liquid-hydrogen tank filling the thruster housing, centered on its nozzle bank. Hydrogen is kept at low pressure, so it doesn't need a cylinder: a chamfered box with internal baffles holds far more in the same space. With its twin, about 180 t usable.

modules.name: Shadow-shield bulkhead
modules.info: Radiation shield between the reactor and the pressurized decks. Engineering's camera looks straight at it.

modules.name: Fusion reactor
modules.info: Main power plant on the centerline, inside its own shield box.

modules.name: Frame-shift drive
modules.info: Hyperspace coil assembly. Wears with each jump.

modules.name: Main drive block
modules.info: Thruster feed, gimbals and the supercruise field generator.

modules.name: Radiator panels (port)
modules.info: Radiator panels laid flush on top of the port thruster housing. They glow on the stern camera when the ship runs hot.

modules.name: Air handlers & water tanks
modules.info: Deckhouse air handling and a day tank of water, aft of the living spaces.

modules.name: Sensor & comms racks
modules.info: Electronics behind the bridge, under the mast.

modules.name: Sensor mast & nav beacon
modules.info: Carries the dorsal camera and a blinking beacon.

modules.name: Surface rover
modules.info: Six-wheeled, two-seat pressurized rover for long ground traverses and heavy sampling: rock cores, drums of ice, crates of specimens. Parked on the bay platform.

modules.name: Fuel scoop intake (ventral)
modules.info: The intake mouth at the front of a fairing faired into the forward belly. The ship skims a star belly-first, so the intake faces the plasma while the windows look away.

modules.name: Survey skiff
modules.info: A small two-seat VTOL flyer for aerial survey: it drops out of the belly bay, maps terrain from the air, grabs samples from places the rover can't reach (cliff faces, ice shelves, the far side of a ravine) and flies them home.

modules.name: Port inboard engine
modules.info: Trim and backup engine, recessed in the inboard housing between the two main banks.

modules.name: Starboard inboard engine
modules.info: Trim and backup engine, recessed in the inboard housing between the two main banks.

modules.name: Telescope turret
modules.info: A 1.2 m survey telescope under a sliding dome on the deck, feeding the observatory below.

modules.name: Reactor shield
modules.info: Borated steel and lithium-hydride shielding on every side of the reactor, with the thicker shadow-shield bulkhead in front of it toward the crew spaces.

modules.name: Lifeboat (starboard)
modules.info: A sealed boat in its own housing on the deck, seating four: the traveler and up to three passengers, for weeks if need be. Boarded by a short ladder from the starboard gallery; it launches sideways through the housing's outboard door.

modules.name: Lifeboat launch door (starboard)
modules.info: The housing's outboard door. It swings down and the boat slides out sideways on rails.

modules.name: Lifeboat (port)
modules.info: A sealed boat in its own housing on the deck, seating four. Boarded by a short ladder from the port gallery; it launches sideways through the housing's outboard door.

modules.name: Lifeboat launch door (port)
modules.info: The housing's outboard door. It swings down and the boat slides out sideways on rails.

modules.name: Port main thruster rim
modules.info: A single shroud round the nozzle bank, following the housing's chamfered section. It runs 0.6 m past the nozzle exits, so the bells are recessed inside it and protected from side impacts and debris.

modules.name: Starboard main thruster rim
modules.info: A single shroud round the nozzle bank, following the housing's chamfered section. It runs 0.6 m past the nozzle exits, so the bells are recessed inside it and protected from side impacts and debris.

modules.info: A quad of small thrusters (up, down, fore and aft, plus one firing outboard) for fine maneuvering: docking, landing and holding attitude while scooping. The pod is faired onto the hull skin.

modules.name: Large hardpoint (ventral, port)
modules.info: Gimballed multi-cannon under the forward belly, fed by a hoist from the magazine. Large hardpoints on a Krait-type hull sit low, so they fire clear of the deck.

modules.name: Large hardpoint (ventral, starboard)
modules.info: Gimballed beam laser under the forward belly, drawing from the power distributor.

modules.name: Medium hardpoint (dorsal, port)
modules.info: Gimballed pulse laser on the forward deck, over the magazine side of the ship.

modules.name: Medium hardpoint (dorsal, starboard)
modules.info: Gimballed pulse laser on the forward deck.

modules.name: Small hardpoint (bow, port)
modules.info: Fixed burst laser between the tines, firing straight down the line of flight.

modules.name: Small hardpoint (bow, starboard)
modules.info: Fixed burst laser between the tines.

modules.name: Utility mount: chaff launcher
modules.info: Throws a cloud of chaff that breaks gimbal and turret locks.

modules.name: Utility mount: heat-sink launcher
modules.info: Ejects a superheated heat sink to dump the ship's heat in seconds, for scooping hot stars or running silent.

modules.name: Utility mount: point defense (port)
modules.info: A small automatic turret that shoots down incoming missiles and mines.

modules.name: Utility mount: point defense (starboard)
modules.info: A small automatic turret that shoots down incoming missiles and mines.

modules.name: Utility mount: wake and survey scanner
modules.info: Reads frame-shift wakes and scans ships and wildlife at range.

modules.name: Utility mount: shield booster
modules.info: Strengthens the shield bubble, fed from the shield generator room.

modules.name: Whip antenna (starboard tine)
modules.info: A long-wave whip antenna swept out and forward from the tine.

modules.name: Blade antenna (starboard tine)
modules.info: A short blade antenna for ship-to-ship and station traffic.

modules.name: Magnetometer boom (starboard tine)
modules.info: A long boom holding the magnetometer well clear of the ship's own fields. A small sensor head sits at its tip.

modules.name: Forward sensor probe (starboard tine)
modules.info: A probe off the tine tip carrying a particle counter and a forward star tracker; the two together make the long-baseline survey pair.

modules.name: Magnetometer head (starboard)
modules.info: The magnetometer at the end of its boom.

modules.name: Whip antenna (port tine)
modules.info: A long-wave whip antenna swept out and forward from the tine.

modules.name: Blade antenna (port tine)

modules.name: Magnetometer boom (port tine)

modules.name: Forward sensor probe (port tine)

modules.name: Magnetometer head (port)
modules.info: The magnetometer at the end of its boom.

modules.name: Comms dish
modules.info: High-gain dish for long-range messages, steered by the comms room. It parks facing up and aft.

modules.name: Navigation sensors
modules.info: Star trackers, the forward lidar and the collision radar, looking out through the bow window between the tines.

modules.name: Shield generator
modules.info: Projects the ship's shield bubble. It soaks up weapon fire and, more often on a survey ship, micrometeoroids and the heat of a close stellar pass. It collapses if overloaded and takes a while to reboot.

exterior.name: Dorsal camera
exterior.info: On the mast, looking forward over the bridge canopy along the whole dorsal hull to the bow prongs. The old hull camera, moved.

exterior.name: Bow camera
exterior.info: On the blunt tip of the starboard tine, looking back along the flank at the deckhouse and tower. The hero shot for arrivals and star skimming.

exterior.name: Scoop camera
exterior.info: On the lip of the scoop fairing, looking forward past the intake.

exterior.name: Stern camera
exterior.info: On the aft face of the deckhouse, looking down over the radiators to the four engines. Engine glow, the radiators running hot, the wake of a jump.

exterior.name: Port flank camera
exterior.info: On the port deck edge aft, looking forward along the port side.

exterior.name: Starboard flank camera
exterior.info: On the starboard deck edge aft, looking forward along the starboard side.

exterior.name: Ventral camera
exterior.info: Under the bow, looking aft along the belly: landing gear, the rover platform going down, the ground coming up on landing.

exterior.name: Rover bay camera
exterior.info: Inside the unpressurized bay, looking across the platform and the rover.

exterior.name: Rover camera
exterior.info: On the rover's mast. Out on the surface it follows the drive; in the bay it looks at the bay door.

exterior.name: Skiff camera
exterior.info: On the skiff's nose. In flight it looks down at the ground it is mapping; in the bay it watches the doors.

windowNotes.hydro: deep in the hull: the window strip becomes a grow-light panel
windowNotes.airlock: the outer door is a floor hatch to the rover bay

windows.name: Bow sensor window
windows.info: An armored optical port across the face between the tines, in front of the navigation sensors.

windows.name: Port gallery skylight
windows.info: A strip of glass in the deck directly over the port gallery.

windows.name: Starboard gallery skylight
windows.info: A strip of glass in the deck directly over the starboard gallery.

windows.name: Sensor windows (port tine)
windows.info: Optical ports in the top of the tine over the survey sensor array.

windows.name: Sensor windows (starboard tine)
windows.info: Optical ports in the top of the tine over the survey sensor array.

windows.name: Starboard gallery windows
windows.info: Glazing in the sloping underside of the starboard wing, along the gallery.

windows.name: Port gallery windows
windows.info: Glazing in the sloping underside of the port wing, along the gallery.

windows.name: Rover bay windows
windows.faces: out to port, below the wing
windows.info: Ports in the port wall of the belly, looking out from the rover bay.

windows.name: Hold windows
windows.faces: out to starboard, below the wing
windows.info: Ports in the starboard wall of the belly, beside the hold.

windows.name: Hydroponics window
windows.info: Daylight for the grow trays: a strip in the sloping starboard flank at the outboard end of the bay.

windows.name: Airlock outer door port
windows.info: The porthole in the airlock's outer door, set in the port flank.

windows.name: Observatory window
windows.info: A wide port beside the telescope controls.

windowShutters: Every window has an armored shutter, including the deckhouse and bridge glazing. Shutters close for supercruise, hyperspace, scooping and anywhere near a strong radiation source, and open when the ship is holding station somewhere safe.
